newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 gold output at 120.6 T - Xinhua.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 gold output at 120.6 T - Xinhua.

text.p: China's gold output totalled 120.6 tonnes last year, the official Xinhua news agency said.
The figure is higher than a recent estimate of 118 tonnes by the official China Gold newspaper.
China produced 108 tonnes of gold in 1995.
Xinhua said the target for the gold industry was to boost production to 150 tonnes a year by the end of the century.
Shandong province in eastern China was the largest producer last year with output of 29 tonnes. Other major producing areas were the provinces of Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, and Inner Mongolia.
It said output rose rapidly in the far northwestern region of Xinjiang, though it gave no details.
Xinhua also said that fixed asset investment in the gold sector was 1.23 billion yuan ($148 million) in 1996. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
Xinhua quoted Jiao Zhi, director of the Gold Control Administration under the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry, as saying that China had verified gold reserves of 4,500 tonnes.
He was quoted as saying, however, that this was not sufficient to meet the fast-growing demand of the industry and he added that China needed to make great efforts to find new sources of gold ore.
Jiao said that the central government was allocating 400 million yuan a year in low-cost loans in order to support gold prospecting.
The official also said that there was no foreign investment in the nation's gold sector now but several projects were under discussion. He did not give details.
